items.headline: Will Capricor’s latest move give deramiocel new life?
items.preview: Capricor is refocusing deramiocel's indication to improve limb function in DMD patients.
items.article:
Capricor Therapeutics Inc. has announced plans to amend its Biologics License Application (BLA) for deramiocel, shifting the focus to improving limb function in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients. This change comes after previous setbacks related to the drug's approval process, which was complicated by an FDA advisory committee's focus on secondary endpoints.

Why this matters: The refocusing of deramiocel's indication aims to realign the drug's approval pathway with primary endpoints, potentially bringing this cell therapy closer to patients in need. Following the announcement, Capricor's shares surged by 58%, reflecting renewed investor interest and optimism about the drug's future prospects.

items.headline: We asked, you answered: Labiotech’s 2026 reader survey results
items.preview: Labiotech's survey reveals insights into its readership and content preferences.
items.article:
Labiotech conducted a survey among its engaged readership to understand their demographics, content preferences, and areas for improvement. The results showed that over 80% of respondents are senior decision-makers in the biotech industry, with a strong preference for newsletters and website articles as their primary content sources.

Why this matters: The feedback highlights the importance of quality content and the need for diverse formats, such as infographics and short videos, to cater to the busy schedules of industry professionals. Labiotech aims to enhance its offerings based on this feedback, ensuring it remains a valuable resource for its audience.

items.headline: DKMS Opens John Hansen Grant: Nearly €1 Million for Blood Cancer Research
items.preview: DKMS invites young scientists to apply for a grant supporting blood cancer research.
items.article:
The DKMS John Hansen Research Grant 2027 is now open for applications, aimed at early-career scientists focusing on innovative approaches to blood cancer treatment. This grant supports research addressing challenges in hematological diseases, including stem cell transplantation and immune complications.

Why this matters: By investing in the next generation of researchers, DKMS seeks to accelerate advancements in blood cancer therapies, ultimately improving patient outcomes and expanding treatment options for various blood disorders.

items.headline: CRISPR roadblocks: Scientists identify genes blocking gene therapy success
items.preview: Researchers discover genes that hinder the effectiveness of gene therapies.
items.article:
A team from the University of Wisconsin–Madison has identified six genes that impede the efficiency of CRISPR-based gene editing. By screening nearly all human genes, they found that knocking out specific genes significantly improved editing outcomes in human cells, particularly in models of genetic eye diseases.

Why this matters: Understanding these genetic roadblocks could lead to enhanced gene therapy strategies, making treatments more effective for various genetic disorders and potentially informing the design of future therapies.

items.headline: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas reveals the emergence of medusa-specific cell states in the Aurelia coerulea scyphozoan
items.preview: New research provides insights into cell type diversification during medusa development.
items.article:
A study published in PLOS Biology presents a single-cell transcriptome atlas of the scyphozoan Aurelia coerulea, detailing the molecular changes during the transition from polyp to medusa. The research highlights an increase in cell type diversity, including the emergence of neural subtypes and striated muscles, which are crucial for the jellyfish's motility.

Why this matters: This work lays the foundation for understanding the evolutionary origins of complex body plans in metazoans and could inform future studies on cell type diversification and development in other organisms.
